nodes.label: Thesis Lock: Packed CPU/edge XNOR + honest STE
nodes.summary: Speedups come from packed kernels on CPU/edge; never claim GPU 32× from sign(); compression 32× ≠ latency; STE trains latents, inference uses pack+popcount.

nodes.label: Honest Dual-Metric Culture
nodes.summary: Always report theoretical word reduction / weight compression separately from measured wall-clock S_compute and S_e2e; never advertise 32×/64× as latency.

nodes.label: bnn-lab (Binary Neural Network Optimiser Lab)
nodes.summary: Installable PyTorch lab (v0.3.0): packed XNOR kernels, wrap/optimise, .bnnpack, vision/audio/seq lanes, repro gates, bridges to BitNet/GGUF/torchao.

nodes.label: World-Class Optimiser v1.0 Bar
nodes.summary: Acceptance gates WC-A/K/O/R/D/P in ROADMAP §1; until all pass, claim only lab/beta.

nodes.label: XNOR–Popcount Dot-Product Identity
nodes.summary: For ±1 vectors with bit0↦+1, bit1↦−1: ⟨w,x⟩ = N − 2·popcount(w⊕x). Pad bits encode +1 so they do not inflate disagreement count.

nodes.label: Amdahl Bound on End-to-End Speedup
nodes.summary: S_e2e = 1/((1−f)+f/S_k). Non-binary layers (softmax, LN, attn, embed) cap e2e gains even when kernel S_k is large.

nodes.label: Memory-Bandwidth Bound Inference
nodes.summary: Large models / batch-1 decode often limited by DRAM bytes/s, not peak FLOPs. 32× denser weights can move kernels from DRAM-bound to L2/L3-bound.

nodes.label: Exact 32× Weight Compression (uint64 pack)
nodes.summary: Aligned binary pack: FP32 4 bytes → 1 bit = 32.00× exact. Gate in golden_floors.json.

nodes.label: Theoretical ~64× Word-Op Reduction
nodes.summary: 64 binary MACs per uint64 XNOR+popcount vs scalar FP32 MAC counting — NOT a wall-clock claim.

nodes.label: Energy Proxy E = P · t
nodes.summary: Board Joules closed-by-proxy: measured wrap latency × assumed power brackets + lit anchors. RAPL optional on Linux; Windows stays proxy.

nodes.label: Fake Binary: sign() + FP GEMM
nodes.summary: PyTorch w.sign() @ x.sign() still uses FP32 GEMM — no packing → no speedup, often slowdown (extra sign kernels). Negative control in benches.

nodes.label: Accuracy Collapse from Information Loss
nodes.summary: sign destroys magnitude; deep binary stacks lose capacity (historically 10–20+ pp ImageNet).

nodes.label: STE Gradient Mismatch
nodes.summary: True ∂sign/∂x = 0 a.e.; STE pretends identity on |x|≤1 → suboptimal minima risk.

nodes.label: GPU Tensor Cores Beat Naive XNOR
nodes.summary: On A100/H100, FP16/BF16/FP8/INT8 Tensor Cores dominate; unoptimized binary popcount rarely beats cuDNN/cuBLAS end-to-end.

nodes.label: Binarizing Stem/Head Trap
nodes.summary: Stem/head are small compute but critical for accuracy; always keep FP or ≥8-bit.

nodes.label: PTQ-Only Ternary LLM Quality Wipe
nodes.summary: Absmean-PTQ or direct QAT of chat Llama into {-1,0,1} without SubLN/CPT/distill is unstable; BitDistill shows gaps ~14 pp that **widen** with scale (0.6B→4B). Sub-4-bit PTQ (GPTQ/AWQ alone) also collapses quality. Use BitDistill recipe or train BitNet from scratch. Lab F13 / docs/23 already warn — cite 2510.13998 numbers.

nodes.label: Stock NPU: No Native 1-bit
nodes.summary: Qualcomm HTP / Apple ANE / Arm Ethos-U are INT8/INT4/FP16-first; native XNOR not drop-in.

nodes.label: Binarized Neural Networks (Courbariaux et al. 2016)
nodes.summary: Foundational W+A ±1 with STE; GPU kernel demo era.

nodes.label: XNOR-Net (Rastegari et al. ECCV 2016)
nodes.summary: Channel-wise scaling α; claims ~58× faster conv ops and 32× memory on ImageNet AlexNet class.

nodes.label: Bi-Real Net (Liu et al. ECCV 2018 / IJCV)
nodes.summary: 1-bit CNN with full-precision identity shortcuts around every binary conv (≈2× real-valued paths vs BinaryNet). ApproxSign piecewise-polynomial STE. ImageNet ResNet-18: 56.4% top-1 / 79.5% top-5 (vs XNOR-Net 51.2% / BinaryNet 42.2% / FP ResNet-18 ~69.3%). ResNet-34: 62.2% top-1 / 83.9% top-5. Codes: github.com/liuzechun/Bi-Real-net. Lab uses Bi-Real residuals on MNIST/CIFAR proxies; full ImageNet train is ACCEPTED-NON-GOAL.

nodes.label: ReActNet (Liu et al. ECCV 2020)
nodes.summary: Generalizes Sign→RSign and PReLU→RPReLU (learnable channel-wise thresholds/slopes) + distributional KL loss vs real teacher. MobileNetV1-based ReActNet-A: **69.4%** ImageNet top-1 at **0.87×10^8 OPs** (~3.0 pp below real MobileNet twin 72.4%). ReActNet-B 70.1% @ 1.63e8 OPs; ReActNet-C 71.4% @ 2.14e8 OPs. ReAct on Bi-Real-18 → 65.5% (+9.1 pp). Comparison anchors: XNOR 51.2%, Bi-Real-18 56.4%, Real-to-Binary 65.4%, MeliusNet29 65.8%. Two-step training (acts then W+A). Code: github.com/liuzechun/ReActNet. Lab docs say '~71% claimed' — precise figures: A=69.4, C=71.4.

nodes.label: IR-Net (Qin et al. CVPR 2020)
nodes.summary: Information Retention Network; Error Decay Estimator (EDE) / tanh-soft STE schedule.

nodes.label: XNOR-Net++ (Bulat & Tzimiropoulos BMVC 2019)
nodes.summary: Learned fused scale factors instead of analytic α; up to ~6% ImageNet gain vs XNOR-Net.

nodes.label: BiBERT: Accurate Fully Binarized BERT (Qin et al. 2022)
nodes.summary: Qin et al. arXiv:2203.06390 — first accurate **W1 E1 A1** BERT. Failure diagnosis: (1) attention-weight information collapse under direct Sign; (2) distillation direction mismatch when using products of two binary activations. Fixes: **Bi-Attention** (maximize entropy of binary attention reps) + **Direction-Matching Distillation (DMD)**. Claims **56.3×** FLOPs and **31.2×** size savings; beats BinaryBERT W1A1 by ~20.4 pp avg GLUE and Q2BERT W2A8 by ~13.3 pp. Lab docs mention BiBERT briefly — strengthen with these failure modes and numbers.

nodes.label: BitNet: Scaling 1-bit Transformers (Wang et al. 2023)
nodes.summary: Wang et al. replace nn.Linear with BitLinear (1-bit weights, higher-bit acts). Foundational proof that Transformers can train with extreme weight quantization. arXiv:2310.11453. Superseded for quality by ternary BitNet b1.58; keep distinction: original BitNet ≈ ±1, b1.58 adds 0.

nodes.label: BitNet b1.58 (Ma et al. 2024)
nodes.summary: Ternary {−1,0,1} weights; matches FP16 LLaMA-class from ~3B+ at equal tokens; memory ~3.55×, latency ~2.71× at 3B; 0 enables feature gating.

nodes.label: 1-bit AI Infra / bitnet.cpp (Wang et al. 2024)
nodes.summary: Wang et al. arXiv:2410.16144 — ternary CPU kernels (TL1/TL2) vs llama.cpp FP16. **Cite carefully with device+thread context:** Apple M2 Ultra unlimited threads: speedup **1.37×–5.07×** (125M→70B); Intel i7-13700H: **2.37×–6.17×**. Energy J/token savings: M2 **55.4%/64.6%/70.0%** (700M/7B/70B); i7 **71.9%/82.2%** (700M/7B). 100B ternary on M2 ~6.58 tok/s unlimited (human-reading class). Lossless vs FP32 kernel on WildChat token match (TL1/TL2 100% vs TQ1_0 1.4%). ACL follow-up arXiv:2502.11880. Official HF: microsoft/bitnet-b1.58-2B-4T (+gguf). Lab docs cite ranges correctly; add hardware footnotes + J/token table.

nodes.label: BitNet a4.8 (Wang et al. 2024)
nodes.summary: Wang/Ma/Wei hybrid: INT4 (or FP4) activations into attention/FFN inputs; TopK sparsify + INT8 on intermediate states (attn out-proj, FFN down). Continue-train from W1.58A8 → W1.58A4 (e.g. 95B+5B tokens). Matches b1.58 quality at same token budget; ~**55%** activated params (7B: 3.4B active); supports **3-bit KV** with negligible avg loss. Enables INT4/FP4 kernels. arXiv:2411.04965. Follow-on: BitNet v2 (arXiv:2504.18415) native 4-bit acts + Hadamard.

nodes.label: BitNet b1.58 2B4T Technical Report (2025)
nodes.summary: Official 2.4B BitNet b1.58 trained 4T tokens (arXiv:2504.12285). Variants: safetensors, bf16, gguf. Primary public checkpoint for bitnet.cpp demos. Prefer this over unofficial PTQ '1-bit' conversions.

nodes.label: BitNet Distillation / BitDistill (Wu et al. 2025)
nodes.summary: Wu et al. arXiv:2510.13998 — convert off-the-shelf FP LLMs (Qwen3 0.6–4B) to 1.58-bit for **task-specific** finetune without full BitNet pretrain. Three stages: (1) SubLN before MHSA/FFN out-projections; (2) continue-pretrain ~10B Falcon tokens; (3) CE + KL logits distill (τ=5) + MiniLM-style multi-head attention-relation distill (prefer **single late layer**). Naive BitNet-SFT gaps ~13–15 pp and worsen with scale; BitDistill recovers FP16-SFT parity on MNLI/QNLI/SST-2 and CNNDM ROUGE while claiming ~**10×** memory and **~2.65×** CPU tok/s (paper table: 427→1135 tok/s, 1.20→0.11 G). Complementary to GPTQ/AWQ init. Distinct from BitDistiller (arXiv:2402.10631, sub-4-bit self-distill).

nodes.label: Sparse-BitNet (2026)
nodes.summary: Zhang et al. arXiv:2603.05168 — ternary BitNet naturally ~42% zeros; more N:M-friendly than BF16. Sparse-BitLinear: magnitude mask from master weights each step, quant-then-mask, **dual STE** (gradients through masked weights). At 2:4, BF16 +18.8% norm PPL vs BitNet +5.7%; BitNet collapses later under N:8 sweeps. Custom 6:8 sparse TC kernels: up to **~1.30×** e2e on Qwen2.5-3B. Related: Q-Sparse (arXiv:2407.10969). Lab mentions Sparse-BitNet once — add these deltas.

nodes.label: Larq Compute Engine (Bannink et al. 2020)
nodes.summary: Fastest open BNN inference engine of its era; ARM BGEMM 8.5–18.5× vs FP on Pixel-class.

nodes.label: FINN (Umuroglu et al. FPGA'17)
nodes.summary: Umuroglu et al. streaming heterogeneous dataflow for BNNs on Zynq. Optimizations: XNOR+popcount MVTU; BN+sign→thresholds; maxpool→OR. ZC706 @~200 MHz wall power: **SFC-max MNIST 12.3M FPS**, 0.31 µs latency, Pchip 7.3 W / Pwall 21.2 W → **~583k FPS/W wall** / **~1.69M FPS/W chip**; LFC-max 1.56M FPS; **CNV-max CIFAR-10/SVHN 21.9k FPS**, 283 µs, Pchip 3.6 W / Pwall 11.7 W → **~1.87k FPS/W wall**. Modern FINN: Brevitas→ONNX→FINN IR→HLS/RTL; github.com/Xilinx/finn. Lab docs cite FPS class correctly; add FPS/W and power rails.
nodes.note: Classic FPGA'17; arXiv companion commonly cited as 1612.07119

nodes.label: Litespark Inference (2026)
nodes.summary: Dade et al. arXiv:2605.06485 — SIMD ternary CPU kernels (Litespark-Inference). Paper claims large speedups vs naive PyTorch on Apple Silicon / x86. Not reproduced in this lab; local numbers stay OpenGap (gap_litespark_local). Do not copy paper × as goldens.

Best stock path for mobile **CPU** W+A binary CNNs. Not a BitNet LLM stack.

End-to-end: train in Brevitas → tidy/streamline → HW layers → fold for FPS target → Vivado/PYNQ deploy. Preferred industrial vision edge path when FPGA available. Heavy vs this repo's teaching kernels.

nodes.label: Goal × Hardware Decision Tree
nodes.summary: GPU datacenter LLM serve (2024–2026): prefer FP8/INT4 via torchao, AWQ, GPTQ, vLLM/TensorRT — Tensor Cores beat research XNOR. AWQ protects salient weights via activation magnitude (~1% channels); GPTQ second-order weight fit — GPTQ can overfit calib domain more than AWQ. CPU/edge LLM: BitNet b1.58 + bitnet.cpp. Mobile NPU: stock INT8/INT4, not XNOR. Vision MCU/FPGA fixed topology: FINN/Larq binary. Hybrid: PTQ INT4 for GPU API + ternary FFN on CPU rare; usually pick one stack. Binary rarely wins end-to-end on NVIDIA TC GPUs (arXiv:1911.04477).

nodes.label: Bi-Real Net (ECCV 2018 / IJCV)
nodes.summary: 1-bit CNN with full-precision identity shortcuts around every binary conv (≈2× real-valued paths vs BinaryNet). ApproxSign piecewise-polynomial STE. ImageNet ResNet-18: 56.4% top-1 / 79.5% top-5 (vs XNOR-Net 51.2% / BinaryNet 42.2% / FP ResNet-18 ~69.3%). ResNet-34: 62.2% top-1 / 83.9% top-5. Codes: github.com/liuzechun/Bi-Real-net. Lab uses Bi-Real residuals on MNIST/CIFAR proxies; full ImageNet train is ACCEPTED-NON-GOAL.

nodes.label: Real-to-Binary Network (ICLR 2020)
nodes.summary: Martinez et al. train binary ResNet-18 via progressive attention matching to a real teacher + data-driven gating/re-scaling of binary-conv outputs using pre-binarization real activations. ImageNet top-1 **65.4%** / top-5 **86.2%** (strong baseline alone 60.9%); FP ResNet-18 69.3% → ~3.9 pp gap. CIFAR-100 Real-to-Bin** 76.2%. arXiv:2003.11535; OpenReview BJg4NgBKvH; code github.com/brais-martinez/real2binary. Often cited loosely as 'Real-to-Bin' without ID — strengthen all lab refs to this paper.

nodes.label: ReActNet (ECCV 2020)
nodes.summary: Generalizes Sign→RSign and PReLU→RPReLU (learnable channel-wise thresholds/slopes) + distributional KL loss vs real teacher. MobileNetV1-based ReActNet-A: **69.4%** ImageNet top-1 at **0.87×10^8 OPs** (~3.0 pp below real MobileNet twin 72.4%). ReActNet-B 70.1% @ 1.63e8 OPs; ReActNet-C 71.4% @ 2.14e8 OPs. ReAct on Bi-Real-18 → 65.5% (+9.1 pp). Comparison anchors: XNOR 51.2%, Bi-Real-18 56.4%, Real-to-Binary 65.4%, MeliusNet29 65.8%. Two-step training (acts then W+A). Code: github.com/liuzechun/ReActNet. Lab docs say '~71% claimed' — precise figures: A=69.4, C=71.4.

nodes.label: ImageNet 1-bit CNN accuracy ladder
nodes.summary: Canonical ImageNet top-1 ladder for W1A1 (unless noted): BinaryNet 42.2% → XNOR-Net 51.2% → Bi-Real-18 56.4% → Real-to-Binary 65.4% → ReActNet-A 69.4% / ReActNet-C 71.4%. OPs metric = BOPs/64 + FLOPs. Lab should cite this ladder instead of vague 'within 3% of FP MobileNet' alone.

nodes.label: BitNet (1-bit Transformer, 2023)
nodes.summary: Wang et al. replace nn.Linear with BitLinear (1-bit weights, higher-bit acts). Foundational proof that Transformers can train with extreme weight quantization. arXiv:2310.11453. Superseded for quality by ternary BitNet b1.58; keep distinction: original BitNet ≈ ±1, b1.58 adds 0.

nodes.label: BitNet b1.58 (Ma et al., 2024)
nodes.summary: Ternary weights {-1,0,1} via absmean RoundClip; 8-bit activations; LLaMA-alike (RMSNorm, SwiGLU, RoPE, no bias). At equal size+100B RedPajama tokens: 3B BitNet matches FP16 LLaMA twin (PPL 9.91 vs 10.04; avg zero-shot 50.2 vs 49.7) with **3.55×** less memory and **2.71×** lower latency (FasterTransformer+2-bit Ladder kernel on GPU). 70B: **11×** max batch → **8.9×** throughput vs FP16 on 2×A100. Arithmetic energy model: ~**71.4×** lower matmul energy on 7nm (INT8 add vs FP16 mul/add) — chip model, not SoC. Equivalence heuristic: 13B b1.58 cheaper than 3B FP16; 30B vs 7B; 70B vs 13B. Caveat: headline GPU latency/memory from research kernels; production CPU path is bitnet.cpp.

nodes.label: BitNet a4.8 (4-bit activations, 2024)
nodes.summary: Wang/Ma/Wei hybrid: INT4 (or FP4) activations into attention/FFN inputs; TopK sparsify + INT8 on intermediate states (attn out-proj, FFN down). Continue-train from W1.58A8 → W1.58A4 (e.g. 95B+5B tokens). Matches b1.58 quality at same token budget; ~**55%** activated params (7B: 3.4B active); supports **3-bit KV** with negligible avg loss. Enables INT4/FP4 kernels. arXiv:2411.04965. Follow-on: BitNet v2 (arXiv:2504.18415) native 4-bit acts + Hadamard.

nodes.label: bitnet.cpp / 1-bit AI Infra (2024–2025)
nodes.summary: Wang et al. arXiv:2410.16144 — ternary CPU kernels (TL1/TL2) vs llama.cpp FP16. **Cite carefully with device+thread context:** Apple M2 Ultra unlimited threads: speedup **1.37×–5.07×** (125M→70B); Intel i7-13700H: **2.37×–6.17×**. Energy J/token savings: M2 **55.4%/64.6%/70.0%** (700M/7B/70B); i7 **71.9%/82.2%** (700M/7B). 100B ternary on M2 ~6.58 tok/s unlimited (human-reading class). Lossless vs FP32 kernel on WildChat token match (TL1/TL2 100% vs TQ1_0 1.4%). ACL follow-up arXiv:2502.11880. Official HF: microsoft/bitnet-b1.58-2B-4T (+gguf). Lab docs cite ranges correctly; add hardware footnotes + J/token table.

nodes.label: BitNet Distillation / BitDistill (2025)
nodes.summary: Wu et al. arXiv:2510.13998 — convert off-the-shelf FP LLMs (Qwen3 0.6–4B) to 1.58-bit for **task-specific** finetune without full BitNet pretrain. Three stages: (1) SubLN before MHSA/FFN out-projections; (2) continue-pretrain ~10B Falcon tokens; (3) CE + KL logits distill (τ=5) + MiniLM-style multi-head attention-relation distill (prefer **single late layer**). Naive BitNet-SFT gaps ~13–15 pp and worsen with scale; BitDistill recovers FP16-SFT parity on MNLI/QNLI/SST-2 and CNNDM ROUGE while claiming ~**10×** memory and **~2.65×** CPU tok/s (paper table: 427→1135 tok/s, 1.20→0.11 G). Complementary to GPTQ/AWQ init. Distinct from BitDistiller (arXiv:2402.10631, sub-4-bit self-distill).

nodes.label: 1.58-bit QAT / distill recipe checklist
nodes.summary: Production-leaning path: (A) From-scratch BitNet b1.58 if you control pretrain tokens (≥100B–2T) and need general LLM. (B) BitDistill for downstream: SubLN → short CPT → logits+attention distill; do **not** absmean-PTQ a chat Llama and ship. (C) Gradual λ / STE with absmean ternary + INT8 acts. Keep stem/embed/LM-head higher precision unless proven otherwise. Prefer bitnet.cpp TL kernels for CPU serve. Lab TernaryLinear is pedagogy/size only.

nodes.label: BiBERT (fully binarized BERT, 2022)
nodes.summary: Qin et al. arXiv:2203.06390 — first accurate **W1 E1 A1** BERT. Failure diagnosis: (1) attention-weight information collapse under direct Sign; (2) distillation direction mismatch when using products of two binary activations. Fixes: **Bi-Attention** (maximize entropy of binary attention reps) + **Direction-Matching Distillation (DMD)**. Claims **56.3×** FLOPs and **31.2×** size savings; beats BinaryBERT W1A1 by ~20.4 pp avg GLUE and Q2BERT W2A8 by ~13.3 pp. Lab docs mention BiBERT briefly — strengthen with these failure modes and numbers.

nodes.label: Binary / ternary transformers landscape
nodes.summary: Three distinct lines: (1) BiBERT-style full W/A/E binarization of encoder BERT (hardest — attention). (2) BitNet Transformer: BitLinear replaces Linear; attention softmax/KV usually higher bit. (3) BitNet b1.58 / a4.8 / BitDistill for generative LLMs. Do not conflate GLUE BiBERT wins with LLM chat quality. Lab tiny binary-ViT sketch is pedagogical only.

nodes.label: FINN FPGA BNN framework (FPGA 2017+)
nodes.summary: Umuroglu et al. streaming heterogeneous dataflow for BNNs on Zynq. Optimizations: XNOR+popcount MVTU; BN+sign→thresholds; maxpool→OR. ZC706 @~200 MHz wall power: **SFC-max MNIST 12.3M FPS**, 0.31 µs latency, Pchip 7.3 W / Pwall 21.2 W → **~583k FPS/W wall** / **~1.69M FPS/W chip**; LFC-max 1.56M FPS; **CNV-max CIFAR-10/SVHN 21.9k FPS**, 283 µs, Pchip 3.6 W / Pwall 11.7 W → **~1.87k FPS/W wall**. Modern FINN: Brevitas→ONNX→FINN IR→HLS/RTL; github.com/Xilinx/finn. Lab docs cite FPS class correctly; add FPS/W and power rails.

nodes.label: Larq + Larq Compute Engine
nodes.summary: TF/Keras BNN training (Larq) + TFLite custom ops for ARM BGEMM (LCE). Hand-tuned tiling/vectorization/multithreading; documented 8.5–18.5× class wins on Pixel/RPi vs FP baselines in ecosystem surveys. Upstream Larq archived ~2026 — pin commit / vendor fork. Best stock path for mobile **CPU** W+A binary CNNs. Not a BitNet LLM stack.

nodes.label: Brevitas → FINN (QAT→FPGA)
nodes.summary: Brevitas (Xilinx/AMD): PyTorch QAT/PTQ with per-tensor bitwidth control including 1-bit; QuantConv/Linear/MHA/RNN. Export ONNX into FINN for FPGA dataflow. End-to-end: train in Brevitas → tidy/streamline → HW layers → fold for FPS target → Vivado/PYNQ deploy. Preferred industrial vision edge path when FPGA available. Heavy vs this repo's teaching kernels.

nodes.label: When AWQ/GPTQ/torchao win vs binary/ternary
nodes.summary: GPU datacenter LLM serve (2024–2026): prefer FP8/INT4 via torchao, AWQ, GPTQ, vLLM/TensorRT — Tensor Cores beat research XNOR. AWQ protects salient weights via activation magnitude (~1% channels); GPTQ second-order weight fit — GPTQ can overfit calib domain more than AWQ. CPU/edge LLM: BitNet b1.58 + bitnet.cpp. Mobile NPU: stock INT8/INT4, not XNOR. Vision MCU/FPGA fixed topology: FINN/Larq binary. Hybrid: PTQ INT4 for GPU API + ternary FFN on CPU rare; usually pick one stack. Binary rarely wins end-to-end on NVIDIA TC GPUs (arXiv:1911.04477).

nodes.label: Sparse-BitNet (N:M + 1.58-bit, 2026)
nodes.summary: Zhang et al. arXiv:2603.05168 — ternary BitNet naturally ~42% zeros; more N:M-friendly than BF16. Sparse-BitLinear: magnitude mask from master weights each step, quant-then-mask, **dual STE** (gradients through masked weights). At 2:4, BF16 +18.8% norm PPL vs BitNet +5.7%; BitNet collapses later under N:8 sweeps. Custom 6:8 sparse TC kernels: up to **~1.30×** e2e on Qwen2.5-3B. Related: Q-Sparse (arXiv:2407.10969). Lab mentions Sparse-BitNet once — add these deltas.

nodes.label: Mobile NPU INT8/INT4 reality (not 1-bit)
nodes.summary: Qualcomm HTP/QNN, Apple ANE/CoreML, Arm Ethos-U: document INT8/INT4/FP16 paths — **no stock 1-bit XNOR**. Ternary BitNet on Snapdragon needs custom Hexagon kernels (ENERZAi/QCS6490 class reports). Product tree: phone NPU → INT8; classic BNN CNN → CPU LCE / FPGA FINN; ternary LLM → bitnet.cpp or custom DSP. Aligns with lab docs/20 CLOSED-BY-PROXY.

nodes.label: Failure: attention binarization
nodes.summary: Sign on Q/K/attention maps destroys selective focus (BiBERT analysis: attention-weight information nearly collapses). Distilling using products of two binary activations causes STE direction mismatch (DMD needed). Practical mitigations: keep attention scores / softmax / KV higher bit (BitNet default); Bi-Attention+DMD for full binary BERT; a4.8 uses sparse INT8 intermediates on attn out-proj. Lab F8 Amdahl already notes softmax — elevate attention-specific citations.

nodes.label: Failure: small-K / thin layers
nodes.summary: Packed XNOR–popcount amortizes poorly when inner dim K ≪ 64/128 or layers are stem/head-sized: packing overhead + FP residual ops dominate; measured wall-clock can be <1× vs FP BLAS. Standard recipe: leave first/last layers FP (≥8-bit); only binarize wide matmuls. Lab G15/G18 document re-pack and Python overhead — connect to K-threshold guidance in kernels docs.

nodes.label: Failure: BatchNorm sensitivity in BNNs
nodes.summary: Without BN after binary layers, training almost always fails (discrete noisy acts). Running stats/momentum matter: Larq guides often use momentum ≈0.9. Prefer Adam on latent weights. On FPGA FINN, BN+sign folds to thresholds — training-time BN still required. Lab G7 CLOSED; keep as KG failure node with Larq/FINN citations.

nodes.label: Failure: naive PTQ into ternary BitNet
nodes.summary: Absmean-PTQ or direct QAT of chat Llama into {-1,0,1} without SubLN/CPT/distill is unstable; BitDistill shows gaps ~14 pp that **widen** with scale (0.6B→4B). Sub-4-bit PTQ (GPTQ/AWQ alone) also collapses quality. Use BitDistill recipe or train BitNet from scratch. Lab F13 / docs/23 already warn — cite 2510.13998 numbers.

nodes.label: HF microsoft/bitnet-b1.58-2B-4T
nodes.summary: Official 2.4B BitNet b1.58 trained 4T tokens (arXiv:2504.12285). Variants: safetensors, bf16, gguf. Primary public checkpoint for bitnet.cpp demos. Prefer this over unofficial PTQ '1-bit' conversions.

nodes.label: ScaleQ-1.58 / AYOT (Wang et al. 2026)
nodes.summary: Wang et al. arXiv:2608.01078 — ternary PTQ for reasoning LLMs: Attend to Your Own Thoughts (AYOT) calibration + CAT-Q. Paper reports Qwen3-1.7B ternary >90.52% of BitNet b1.58 2B4T on 4 math/coding tasks with 4M calib tokens, and a Qwen3-4B absolute +8.97% vs that baseline; claims scaling to 235B. Literature only — this lab does not reproduce ScaleQ or treat those figures as goldens. Distinct from naive absmean PTQ wipe.

nodes.summary: Li et al. arXiv:2606.25674 — convert pretrained LLM backbones into BitNet-style text embedders (ternary weights, quantized activations) via contrastive CPT + teacher distillation; MMTEB (eng, v2) experiments on Qwen3-0.6B / Gemma3-270M. Literature only. docs/15 names BitEmbed as an embeddings routing hint — not a lab golden.

Their stack, not this lab. Audio lane remains synthetic pedagogy (decision_nongoal_asr_whisper).
